body:
Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the greatest
painters of all time. He was also a great inventor,
scientist, and musician. Very few people, however,
know that da Vinci was also a creative cook.
In 1473, twenty-year-old da Vinci worked as a
cook at a restaurant in Florence, Italy. When he
took charge of the kitchen, da Vinci changed the
menu completely. (A) He made simple but artistic
dishes like fish with a few carrot slices. Some
dishes were even decorated with flowers. Customers,
however, were ⓐunsatisfied because they were
used to dishes with big servings of meat. ⓑThus,
da Vinci lost his job.
A few years later, da Vinci opened a restaurant
with his friend Sandro Botticelli. He wanted to create
a place where people could try his ⓒuncommon
dishes. They put up a beautifully painted sign and
made a uniquely written menu. Da Vinci believed
that people would soon find his creative food was
ⓓworth trying. ⓔLuckily, that never happened. (B)
In the early 1480s, da Vinci began to work for
Ludovico Sforza in Milan. ㉠Sforza gave him many
different roles, such as a musician, a painter, and
an engineer. ㉡He also put in charge of the
kitchen. Da Vinci did not stop at cooking creative
dishes. ㉢He wanted to cook much more quick and
easy. Thus, he invented new machines for his
kitchen. ㉣He created machines where could crush
vegetables and pull spaghetti. (C) Surely, they were
all very innovative, but most of them were too big
or too difficult to use.
In 1495, Sforza asked da Vinci to make a grand
painting, which was based on the last supper of
Jesus, on the wall of a church in Milan. (D) Da Vinci
gladly took on the project because he had always
been interested in food. ㉤He spent most of his
time cooking all kinds of food to decide what to
put food on the table in his picture. (E) “Da Vinci
has wasted his time in the kitchen for over a year.
㉥That’s why he hasn’t finished the painting yet,”
complained the people from the church to Sforza.
Although da Vinci never became a successful cook,
he showed great interest in cooking throughout his
life. He was not only a great painter but also a
creative cook. (가)Now that you know all about his
secret passion for cooking, you will never look at
The Last Supper the same way.

위 글의 밑줄 친 (가)가 의미하는 바로 적절한 것은?
choices: The Last Supper will help you see that da Vinci was a creative painter.
You’ll find out that The Last Supper is full of da Vinci’s favorite foods to cook.
You’ll be more likely to focus more on the individual characters painted in The Last Supper.
Next time you encounter The Last Supper, you will see how da Vinci’s love for cooking is represented.
When you look at The Last Supper, you’ll see that da Vinci was too ambitious for cooking to finish the painting.

Q. You take beautiful pictures of them, but isn't it
(A)_____________ to take pictures of haenyeo?
At first, they didn't understand why I wanted to
take their pictures. They didn't think they looked
pretty in their wetsuits. I said to them, “You’re very
special. I want to show your culture to the world."
They opened up to me then. Of course, I also
promised them that I would make them look
beautiful in my pictures.
Q. Could you tell us more about haenyeo? What's
so special about them?
I can tell you three things. First, haenyeo are a
(B)_______________ of strong women. Jejudo, which is
a volcanic island, is not suitable for farming, so
many haenyeo have become the breadwinners for
their families. Second, haenyeo form their own
communities and help each other. For example,
more-experienced haenyeo train less-experienced
haenyeo. Third, because they stay in the water
without any breathing devices, haenyeo can't catch
a lot of seafood. This is good for the underwater
environment. Catching too much marine life at one
time in one place can (C)_____________ the ocean.

take their pictures. They didn’t think they looked
pretty in their wetsuits. I said to them, "You're very
special. I want to show your culture to the world."
They opened up to me then. Of course, I also
promised them that I would make them look
beautiful in my pictures.

that never missed its target. The second treasure
